questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Experience living in another European city

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a city in Europe really well. Improving my german skills. Living in a bigger city, a city with a lot of history and a rich cultural life.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. Freie Universität was very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: E-mails from Freie Universität inviting to info-arrangements etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it quite difficult. But a lot of people didn't have as much trouble finding a place as I did. Try Facebook-groups such as "Dansker i Berlin" or WG-Gesucht.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's much more fun to live off campus. Berlin is an amazing city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The first few weeks are quite confusing. You can register for classes at your own institute through Campus Management, and then just show up to other classes that you find in the course catalog. It can be a good idea to just register and show up to a lot of classes the first week and then decide which classes you want to take. Everything will fall into place, you just have to be a bit patient.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Freie Universität will send you lots of emails, and you can also contact them if you have questions. They respond faster than KU.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I registered for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register and attend many classes during the first (or two first) weeks and then decide which classes you want to take. The first week of classes is just information about how the class is structured, the exam, etc. So it's easier to decide which classes to take after the first week.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level is lower than at KU. There are a lot of student presentations and students discussing what they think about topics, while professors don't contribute as much as they do at KU. But the level of critical and independent thinking is higher at Freie Universität.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More student presentations, student participation and student discussions of the texts. The courses can go in many different directions depending on the knowledge etc. of the students. The courses are not as structured as at KU where the professor has a power-point and some key points that they want the students to leave the class with.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Research Design and Methods for Political Science
The Debt is Owed to Us. The Political Economy and Practice of Debt and Dispossession
American Political Development
Political Polarization in the US
Quantitative Methods in Political Science and Area Studies
Critical Political Ecology: Between Marxism and Environmentalism

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Political Polarization in the US. Christian Lammert is a really good professor. You cannot be sure that this particular course will be offered, but he has also talked about a lot of other courses that he wants to offer in the future. 

The Debt is Owed to Us. The Political Economy and Practice of Debt and Dispossession. Really interesting literature and discussions in class (but also because the students knew a lot and had a lot of interesting perspectives). Friederike Beier & Jule Govrin were really good professors, but they did not contribute that much in class.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected costs. You will have to pay for a semester ticket at the beginning of your stay, but this will give you free public transport for the rest of your stay.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Almost everything is cheaper in Berlin. But this can also mean that you spend a lot more money because you want to take advantage of the fact that eating out is cheaper, etc.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't really participate in the Erasmus activities. There were a lot of activities, but not as many as I expected. But I did participate in the sports activities offered by Freie Universität (Contemporary Dance and Bouldering). That was really fun! And a nice opportunity to try something different.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Go to concerts (there are so many good artists playing, and a lot of different venues. You should try to see some German artists as well). There are also some really nice jazz bars. 
The lakes and forests around Berlin are also really nice. 
And there are so many good places to eat! And much cheaper than in Copenhagen. 
There are also a lot of good museums, markets and of course clubs.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
You can spend a lot of time doing all of the above. And you can spend a lot of time getting to know the city, just walking around and experiencing the life, the people, the food, etc.
But there are also a lot of nice cities close to Berlin that you can visit. But I didn't have the time to do that.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It's a bit difficult to socialize with the local students if you don't speak German very well. But group work and sports activities through Freie Universität are a good start.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I can't think of any right now.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The diversity and openness to many different people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the city and choose some interesting courses. But try to experience all the nice things in Berlin and find your way to spend as little time as possible at uni. Exchange is so much more than that.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just to live in Berlin and really get to know the city. Improve my German skills. Meet a lot of amazing people. Have a lot of really cool and interesting cultural experiences.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding a place to live, getting my classes pre-approved by KU, and writing my exams while my next semester at KU had begun.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
